key_concepts: Soil covers most of Earth's land and supports plants, animals, and humans.
Soil is made of small rock particles and decayed plant and animal matter.
Humus is dark organic material from decaying plants and animals.
Soil types differ in color, texture, odor, and ability to hold water.

Loam is a mixture of sand and clay, holds enough water, and is best for planting crops.
Sand has coarse, loose particles and does not hold water well.
Soil is arranged in layers called horizons, forming a soil profile.
The organic layer contains dried leaves, twigs, small rocks, and decaying organisms.
Topsoil is rich in humus and minerals and is soft and porous enough to hold air and water.
Subsoil is poor in humus but rich in minerals and is harder and more compact than topsoil.
